title: Dollar Banknote Emoji 💵 Meaning: Cash, Prices and Pay
description: The 💵 dollar banknote emoji means cash, payment, cost or US dollars. See how people use it for bills, tips and budgets, and how it differs from 💰 and 💸.
summary: The 💵 dollar banknote emoji shows a green bill, or a banded stack of them, marked with a dollar sign. It means cash and day-to-day money matters: paying someone, the price of something, wages, tips and budgets. It also identifies US dollars specifically among the currency emojis.
meaning: This is the working emoji of money talk. It appears when rent is due, when a friend owes for concert tickets, when a seller lists a price or a freelancer sends an invoice. “Send the 💵” is a payment request; “cash only 💵” is a notice at a market stall. Compared with the money bag, it feels transactional and specific.

It is also the emoji for green paper cash as an idea. Songs and slang that talk about “dead presidents,” “green,” “bands” or “racks” get illustrated with 💵, and a row of them is a simple flex about earnings. Captions like “get that 💵” encourage someone to chase a paycheck. In that register it overlaps with the money bag, though the bills suggest cash you can count.

For anyone dealing with multiple currencies, 💵 means USD. Travel bloggers, currency exchange businesses and international sellers use the dollar, euro, pound and yen notes side by side to show which money they are discussing. Outside the United States, many users still pick 💵 as the generic banknote because green dollar bills are so widely recognized.

It has no hidden meaning. The only caution is the company it keeps: like other money emojis, it turns up in spam about easy income, and in posts selling things that should not be sold online. On its own it is as plain as a price tag on a shelf.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Splitting costs is the main use. “You owe me 20 💵” and “I'll bring 💵 for the cover” are typical. It often pairs with a payment app name. Parents and teenagers use it in allowance negotiations, and roommates in the monthly round of bills.

contexts.label: In business posts
contexts.body: Sellers mark prices, discounts and accepted payment types with it. Job ads use it for pay rates, and gig workers post it with screenshots of a good shift's earnings. Budgeting and “cash stuffing” creators, who sort paper money into envelopes, use 💵 as their signature emoji.

contexts.label: On TikTok and Instagram
contexts.body: Money-saving challenges, “how much I made” videos and tipping stories carry it. In music and fashion content it is part of the vocabulary of success, typically stacked several times. Giveaway posts use it to signal a cash prize, which is also a format scammers imitate.

contexts.label: Around the world
contexts.body: Travelers use it when discussing exchange rates or how much cash to carry. In countries where US dollars circulate alongside local money, it can be quite literal. Elsewhere people often swap in the local banknote emoji if one exists, or keep 💵 as the universal sign for cash.

confusedWith.difference: The 💰 money bag implies a fortune, profit or a big score. 💵 is ordinary cash and exact payments. “I got paid” fits either, but “you owe me” belongs to the banknote.
The 💸 money with wings is a bill flying off, used for spending, losses or sending a payment. 💵 is money sitting still: what something costs or what you have.
The 💶 euro banknote stands for euros, as 💷 does for pounds and 💴 for yen. Pick the note that matches the currency you mean; 💵 is specifically dollars and the default for generic cash.

avoid: Don't send 💵 as a reply to someone describing money troubles; it can look like you are making light of them.
Avoid using it to request payment from a client in place of a proper invoice or a clear amount.
design: Platforms draw either a single green bill or a small banded stack, with a dollar sign or a portrait oval at the center. Apple shows a paper-banded bundle; Google and Microsoft have shown flatter single notes. The green color sets it apart from the yen, euro and pound notes, which use other colors.

faqs.q: What does 💵 mean in a text?
faqs.a: Money in a practical sense: a payment owed, a price, wages or cash you need to bring. It rarely carries an emotional or flirtatious meaning.
💵 is cash and specific payments. 💰 is wealth or a large gain. 💸 is money leaving, through spending or loss. Together they cover having money, making it and watching it go.
Its official name specifies a dollar banknote, and in currency contexts it means dollars. In casual chat people everywhere use it for money in general, regardless of local currency.

faqs.q: What does 💵 mean on Snapchat or Instagram stories?
faqs.a: Typically a flex about earnings, a price on something for sale or a call for payment. On giveaway posts it promises a cash prize, so verify the account before sharing any details.

faqs.q: Is the dollar banknote emoji appropriate for work messages?
faqs.a: In casual team chat about expenses or bonuses it is fine. In formal communication about salaries, invoices or budgets, written figures are clearer and more professional.
